response.sql: WITH manager_rates AS (SELECT year, league_id, team_id, COUNT(*) AS record_count, AVG(1.0 * w / NULLIF(g, 0)) AS avg_win_rate FROM manager_half GROUP BY year, league_id, team_id), team_rates AS (SELECT t.team_id, COALESCE(m.record_count, 0) AS record_count, m.avg_win_rate FROM team AS t LEFT JOIN manager_rates AS m ON m.year = t.year AND m.league_id = t.league_id AND m.team_id = t.team_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_win_rate) AS mean_win_rate FROM team_rates) SELECT tr.team_id, tr.avg_win_rate, tr.record_count, tr.avg_win_rate - o.mean_win_rate AS difference FROM team_rates AS tr CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE o.mean_win_rate IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CASE WHEN tr.avg_win_rate IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, difference DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each row in team represents a team season, identified by year, league_id, and team_id. A record with zero games has no defined win rate.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat each distinct team_id as one team across all seasons.
alternatives.sql: WITH team_ids AS (SELECT DISTINCT team_id FROM team), manager_rates AS (SELECT mh.team_id, COUNT(*) AS record_count, AVG(1.0 * mh.w / NULLIF(mh.g, 0)) AS avg_win_rate FROM manager_half AS mh WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM team AS t WHERE t.year = mh.year AND t.league_id = mh.league_id AND t.team_id = mh.team_id) GROUP BY mh.team_id), team_rates AS (SELECT t.team_id, COALESCE(m.record_count, 0) AS record_count, m.avg_win_rate FROM team_ids AS t LEFT JOIN manager_rates AS m ON m.team_id = t.team_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_win_rate) AS mean_win_rate FROM team_rates) SELECT tr.team_id, tr.avg_win_rate, tr.record_count, tr.avg_win_rate - o.mean_win_rate AS difference FROM team_rates AS tr CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE o.mean_win_rate IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CASE WHEN tr.avg_win_rate IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, difference DESC LIMIT 10
